title: investigate-customer-credit-bleed-from-aggregate-rollup-glitch
creator: Liam Chen
description: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported unexpected decreases in their available invoice credits over the last 72 hours. The chargeback/billing rollup shows residual negative adjustments attributed to a mid-night aggregate job that merges hourly meter snapshots. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and fix for the aggregate-rollup credit bleed that caused customer-visible billing deltas.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate high concurrent request volume for a single tenant (500 reqs/sec) spanning 00:00-01:00 UTC
2) Ensure KV-cache hits > 70% to produce non-trivial prefix caching behavior
3) Trigger hourly aggregation job 'billing-rollup-v2' scheduled at 01:05 UTC
4) Observe resulting per-tenant invoice_credit_delta metrics and cross-check with per-request token_cost logs
5) In affected tenants, you will see invoice_credit_delta negative deltas not matched to any recorded request_id entries (missing token-accounting entries).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Pager received from account team: customer 'Acme Edge' complaining about sudden 12% credit drop.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Correlated Grafana dashboard (billing/rollup-variance) shows spikes in 'rollup_rewrite_events' at 01:05 UTC and 13:05 UTC for multiple regions.
2026-03-10 13:45 - Examined hourly rollup job logs: noticed 'merge_v2' path re-processed previously compacted partial_hour shards when leader election occurred during job runtime.

2026-03-10 15:20 - Found gap: token accounting records for some request_ids were present in 'realtime-metering' but omitted in the 'compact-shard' microbatch due to a race with TTL-based shard eviction.

2026-03-11 09:05 - Hypothesis: a race condition between the compact-shard worker and the rollup-merger causes double-subtraction in aggregate output when the merger replays an already-applied negative adjustment for retries.
2026-03-11 11:30 - Reproduced locally by creating synthetic shard files with overlapping sequence ranges and forcing leader failover; observed invoice_credit_delta double-applied in rollup output.

2026-03-12 08:00 - Cross-checked Dedicated and Private logs: Dedicated had identical symptom but lower amplitude; Private customers running on air-gapped package had delayed manifestation because of staggered cron timezones.

2026-03-12 14:10 - Temporary mitigation applied: rollup job flag 'strict-verify' enabled which skips any merge that doesn't pass sequence-continuity checks; this stops new incorrect deltas but leaves historic incorrect adjustments unresolved.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Ran a dry-run repair script that recomputes aggregates for the last 48 hrs for 5 affected tenants. Dry-run matches expected tokens, confirming reconstruction approach is viable.
2026-03-13 12:25 - Customer comms: Billing team prepared interim credits for top 3 affected customers while we finalize the repair and code fix. Customer success notified impacted tenants.
temporary_mitigations: Enabled rollup job flag 'strict-verify' (prevents merges with sequence gaps) — applied to hosted control plane and Dedicated orchestration jobs.
Instructed Private package owners to apply hotfix script to schedule (patch v0.21.3) that toggles strict-verify for local cron jobs.
Provisioned manual credits for top 3 affected customers (finance ticket FIN-4982) pending final reconciliation.
resolution_plan: 1) Code fix: add idempotent-merge semantics to billing-rollup-merger: add per-tenant applied-change watermark plus sequence-range reconciliation before applying negative/positive adjustments (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4398).
2) Add end-to-end integration test that simulates leader failover during merge with overlapping shards (unit + integration harness).
3) Run repair job to recompute aggregates for 72-hour window for all tenants that show non-zero 'orphan_adjustments' — schedule in low-traffic window and throttle to avoid DB IO storm.
4) Release hotfix to Hosted control plane and Dedicated pools; publish Private package v0.21.3 and notify customers via private channel.
5) Follow-up monitoring: add rollup-consistency alert and a daily job that validates rollup outputs against raw per-request token accounting for top 200 tenants.
test_plan: - Unit tests validating idempotent-merge behavior with synthetic overlapping shard inputs.
- Integration test in staging simulating leader election during merge (use chaos-monkey to kill leader mid-merge).
- Backfill dry-run on staging using real-week sample to confirm repair logic before production run.
- Post-deploy smoke check: validate invoice_credit_delta per-tenant matches realtime-metering within 0.01% for sampled tenants over 24h.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): deploy idempotent-merge to hosted control plane and Dedicated on canary nodes (10%) with strict-verify turned on — monitor for 4h.
Phase 2 (full): if no regressions, deploy to 100% and push Private package v0.21.3 to repos; notify private customers about upgrade window.
Repair: run recompute job in batches of 50 tenants/hour to reconcile historical deltas; notify finance when each batch completes.
postmortem_actions: - Implement per-tenant applied-change watermark persisted with rollup state to prevent re-application.
- Update runbook for rollup jobs to include leader election safety checks and an explicit quiesce window.
- Add billing reconciliation dashboard panels and an alert for 'orphan_adjustments' > 0.5% of daily credit usage.
- Schedule a cross-team review (Billing, Serving Runtime, Reliability) to propose longer-term architecture changes (shard ownership guarantees).
notes_for_support: If customers report small mismatches (<0.5%), advise that strict-verify has been enabled and that historic corrections are queued for repair.
For Private customers: provide the v0.21.3 package and one-off assistance to run recompute if they cannot schedule during low-traffic hours.
Escalate any new customer reports to on-call SRE and tag this ticket.
